title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.23970v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. However, different manipulation intentions can lead to substantially different hand trajectories even when interacting with the same object. Existing methods have not sufficiently explored the intrinsic relationships between articulated hand movements and object semantics to capture such operation-dependent motion patterns. Therefore, we propose TOMAS, a topology-aware operation modeling and adaptive staging framework for egocentric hand forecasting. Specifically, we develop a topology-aware hand-object reasoning mechanism that associates hand skeletal structures and articulation dynamics with object semantics and spatial relationships to jointly infer potential interaction targets and latent manipulation operations. The resulting object-operation representations provide interaction conditions

translated_title: TOMAS：面向第一视角手部预测的拓扑感知操作建模与自适应分期
translated_abstract: 从第一视角视频中预测未来的手部运动，在理解人类意图和手-物体交互方面发挥着重要作用。然而，即使与同一物体进行交互，不同的操作意图也会导致截然不同的手部运动轨迹。现有方法尚未充分探索铰接式手部运动与物体语义之间的内在关系，难以捕捉这种依赖于操作的运动模式。因此，我们提出了TOMAS，一个面向第一视角手部预测的拓扑感知操作建模与自适应分期框架。具体而言，我们开发了一种拓扑感知的手-物体推理机制，将手部骨骼结构和关节动态与物体语义及空间关系相关联，从而联合推断潜在的交互目标和隐含的操作。所得到的物体-操作表示为交互提供了条件。
tldr: 该论文提出TOMAS框架，通过拓扑感知的手-物体推理机制将手部骨骼结构与物体语义相关联，并采用自适应分期策略，从而捕捉依赖操作意图的运动模式，实现第一视角视频中手部未来运动的预测。
